classification.difficultyReason: Form a quadratic area model from two variable side lengths, restrict it to positive dimensions, and use its graph to interpret the maximum area.

content.prompt:
Justify any conclusions and/or assumptions made in the context of the problem.

A rectangle is shown below.

spec.description: Unshaded rectangle, horizontal side labelled 25-x and right vertical side labelled 3x; no units supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied side expressions are shown.

children.prompt: Develop an equation and then use a graph to determine the maximum area of the rectangle.

answer.short:
$A=3x(25-x)=-3x^2+75x$, for $0<x<25$. The maximum area is $468.75$ square units, at $x=12.5$.

This is the highest point on the area graph.
answer.worked:
Both side lengths must be positive, so $0<x<25$.
$$\begin{align*}A&=(25-x)(3x)\\A&=-3x^2+75x\end{align*}$$
Plot $A=-3x^2+75x$ over $0<x<25$. The graph has its maximum at $(12.5,468.75)$.
$$\begin{align*}A(12.5)&=3(12.5)(25-12.5)\\A(12.5)&=468.75\end{align*}$$
The maximum area is $468.75$ square units. The side lengths are $12.5$ and $37.5$ units.
